# Every research claim hwde holds, and what it found

| Claim | Paper | Verdict | What hwde found | Evidence or plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/1` A 47 uF capacitor with 0.2 nH ESL and 0.1 mOhm ESR resonates at 1.64 MHz, where /Z/ is its ESR. | [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) | reproduced | check_pdn_z's branch model puts the minimum at 1.64 MHz (within 1 %) and /Z/ = ESR there. | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_single_capacitor_series_resonance |
| `impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/2` Two parallel capacitors anti-resonate at f1 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(Lb Cp)) with /Z/ = sqrt(Lb/Cp) there. | [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) | partial | The peak sits at 1/(2 pi sqrt((Lb+Lp) Cp)): f1 holds only while Lp << Lb (19 % off at Lp = Lb/2). Its height is X^2/(Rb+Rp), here 2.7x sqrt(Lb/Cp), not sqrt(Lb/Cp). | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_antiresonance_frequency_holds_magnitude_does_not |
| `impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/3` A higher-ESR (lower-Q) decoupling capacitor lowers the anti-resonance spike. | [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) | partial | True until the two branches' ESR add up to about sqrt((Lb+Lp)/Cp); past that the spike is gone and more ESR raises /Z/ over the whole band. | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_lower_q_lowers_antiresonance |
| `impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/4` n identical capacitors in parallel keep the resonance frequency and lower /Z/ by n. | [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) | reproduced | Exactly, in the lumped model (mounting inductance shared between them would break it; check_pdn_z gives each its own). | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_n_identical_caps_divide_impedance |
| `practical-considerations-designing-reliable-dc-2020/1` X7R MLCCs lose 80 % of their capacitance at 80 % of rated voltage. | [Practical Considerations for Designing Reliable DC/DC Converters, Applied to a BIPV Case](https://doi.org/10.3390/en13040834) | partial | Secondhand (the review repeats [52]). lib/mlcc.py's generic curve, fitted to makers' curves, agrees for a 10 uF/10 V 0603 at 8 V (79 % lost) but gives 29 % for a 100 nF/50 V 0603 at 40 V: the loss follows capacitance per volume. | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_mlcc_80pct_bias_loss_holds_for_dense_parts_only |
| `design-thermal-characterization-printed-circuit-2026/1` IPC-2152 (external, 1 oz, dT 10 C) rates 0.10/0.15/0.20/0.25 mm tracks at 0.30/0.50/0.72/1.02 A. | [Design and thermal characterization of printed circuit board trace fuse elements for overcurrent protection in miniaturized wireless IoT sensor node circuits](https://doi.org/10.22271/27084477.2026.v7.i2a.113) | refuted | check_current's IPC-2152 table gives 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50 A: the paper's ratings are 1.5-2x higher, and grow 3.4x for 2.5x the width where any IPC model grows slower than the cross-section (IPC-2221: 1.94x). | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_trace_fuse_ratings_disagree_with_ipc2152 |
| `design-thermal-characterization-printed-circuit-2026/2` Blow time scales as (I/I_rated)^-1.7 at 1.5-2x overload and ^-2.3 at 3-4x. | [Design and thermal characterization of printed circuit board trace fuse elements for overcurrent protection in miniaturized wireless IoT sensor node circuits](https://doi.org/10.22271/27084477.2026.v7.i2a.113) | refuted | The paper's own Table 1 gives exponents of 3.1-3.4 at 1.5-2x and 3.8-4.0 at 3-4x, on every width. | tests/test_research_claims.py::test_trace_fuse_blow_time_exponent_contradicts_its_table |
| `design-thermal-characterization-printed-circuit-2026/3` A 35 um trace fuse opens at an average of 284 C (peak 219-327 C), far below copper's melting point. | [Design and thermal characterization of printed circuit board trace fuse elements for overcurrent protection in miniaturized wireless IoT sensor node circuits](https://doi.org/10.22271/27084477.2026.v7.i2a.113) | untested |  | A trace-fuse coupon board (designed, not ordered: the EE map's test boards) with 0.10-0.25 mm necks, blown on a bench supply; until then hwde treats a trace as a fuse only by the adiabatic Onderdonk melt estimate, never this paper's numbers. |
| `parasitic-loop-inductances-reduction-pcb-2021/1` A vertical (double-sided) GaN commutation loop has about 3x less inductance than a lateral one: 4.85 vs 12.35 nH measured at 10 MHz. | [Parasitic Loop Inductances Reduction in the PCB Layout in GaN-Based Power Converters Using S-Parameters and EM Simulations](https://doi.org/10.3390/en14051495) | untested |  | Rebuild both loops from the paper's Fig. 2 dimensions and extract them with a quasi-static inductance solver (task 261031-012434-e34f3046f2's extraction wrappers); hwde should land within 20 % of the measured values, and the ratio within 15 %. |
